This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner Kumuda Ranjan Panda, son of Padmanav Panda for quashing the judgment and order dated 07.10.2024 passed by the opposite party no.3- Presiding Officer, Land Acquisition Rehabilitation & Resettlement Authority, Berhampur in LAR & R Case No.09 of 2020 under Annexure-10 with a further prayer to direct the opposite party no.3 to award the compensation share in favour of the petitioner.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Rehabilitation & Resettlement Authority, Berhampur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The impugned order indicates that the dispute arose to the apportionment of the awarded compensation in L.A. Case No.74 of 2015, which has been referred to the Court of LAR & R Authority, Berhampur under section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation & Resettlement Act, 2013 by the Collector -cum- L.A.O., Ganjam,
Chatrapur for settlement and accordingly, LAR & R Case No.09 of 2020 was registered.
After assessing the evidence adduced and the oral evidence so also documentary evidence, the Court was of the view that Padmanav Panda (father of the petitioner) and his wife Dinamani Panda (mother of the petitioner) had purchased the acquired land out of their income and during the Kumuda Ranjan Panda vs State Of Odisha And Others ..... ... on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190824499/
1 lifetime of Dinamani Panda, she had sold a portion of her purchased land along with her husband Padmanav Panda to Bipra Charan Panigrahi and others and that apart, the deceased Dinamani executed willnama in respect of the acquired land and other lands of her in favour of her husband Padmanav Panda and therefore, it was held that the disbursement of the compensation amount only for the reason of pending of the Civil Suit is not acceptable and moreover, Padmanav Panda is alive and therefore, the petitioner was not entitled to any portion of the awarded compensation and thus,
the Court directed that the awarded compensation be disbursed in favour of Padmanav Panda for the land and structure existed over the acquired land to the extent of Ac.0.030 decimals and the awarded compensation for the acquired land to the extent of Ac.0.019 decimals in favour of Sibaram Panigrahi.

sentences.text:
As it appears the petitioner instituted Civil Suit No.209 of 2011 in the Court of Senior Civil Judge,
Berhampur seeking partition of the suit schedule property comprising of movable and immovable properties of the Hindu undivided family, available with the Karta Padmanav Panda and his wife Dinamani Panda through the process of the Court and after taking evidence from both the sides,
both oral as well as documentary, the Court was of the view that the plaintiff (petitioner) has not adduced a single Record of Right suggesting therein that the right in respect of the suit schedule property had devolved upon his father Padmanav from his predecessor in interest and there is no documentary proof to suggest the antecedent title in favour of the forefathers of Padmanav so that the plaintiff (petitioner) can put forth his claim for partition of the suit schedule properties.

entities.text:
Court of Senior Civil Judge,
Berhampur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: On the other hand, the plaintiff (petitioner) by his own admission accepted the fact that the defendant no.1 i.e. Padmanav Panda being engaged in Government service and having left the same, pursued agricultural business as his avocation with lucrative profit and therefore, the attending facts and circumstances leads to an irresistible conclusion that the suit schedule property was the self- acquired property of Padmanav Panda and since the suit schedule properties were the individual acquisition of Padmanav Panda, the plaintiff (petitioner) cannot as a matter of right to seek partition of the same as Padmanav Panda can deal with the property as per his own choice.
Accordingly, the suit was dismissed.

It appears that the petitioner has challenged the said judgment and order passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge, Berhampur, Ganjam before the learned District Judge, Ganjam, Berhampur in R.F.A. No.134 of 2024, which is subjudice.

After hearing the learned counsel for both the parties and carefully going through the reasons assigned by the opposite party no.3 in the impugned judgment and order dated 07.10.2024, we find no illegality or impropriety in the same.
Accordingly, the writ petition being devoid of merits, stands dismissed.
( S.K. Sahoo) Judge ( Chittaranjan Dash) Judge 02.
In view of the order passed today in W.P.(C) No.29752 of 2024, this I.A. is disposed of.
